source.text: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἀκούσαντες ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ εἶπαν· Σκληρός ἐστιν ὁ λόγος οὗτος· τίς δύναται αὐτοῦ ἀκούειν;

records.literal_gloss: Many therefore having heard of the disciples of him said, "Hard is the word this; who is able it to hear?"

en.L: So many of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, when they heard [this], said, "This word is hard; who is able to listen to it?"
en.B: When they heard this, many of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples said, "This message is harsh. Who can bear to listen to it?"
en.R: Many of Jesus's disciples heard this and said, "These words are too hard to take. Who can keep listening to them?"

es.L: Así que muchos de sus discípulos, al oír[lo], dijeron: «Dura es esta palabra; ¿quién puede escucharla?».
es.B: Al oír esto, muchos de sus discípulos dijeron: «Este mensaje es duro. ¿Quién puede soportar escucharlo?».
es.R: Muchos de los discípulos de Jesús oyeron esto y dijeron: «Estas palabras son demasiado duras. ¿Quién puede seguir escuchándolas?».

decisions.choice: his disciples: the wider circle of people who followed Jesus, not only the Twelve
decisions.reason: John uses "disciples" of everyone who had attached themselves to Jesus as their teacher. The Twelve are named as a separate, smaller group a few verses later (6:67), after many of these disciples have left (6:66). Those who object here are followers, not the crowd of 6:41 and 6:52.

decisions.choice: hard: harsh and offensive, hard to accept
decisions.reason: The word describes something rough or severe, not something obscure. The disciples' difficulty is not that they cannot follow Jesus's meaning but that they cannot stomach it: he has just said that unless they eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood they have no life in them (6:53-58).

decisions.choice: listen to it: hear the word with acceptance
decisions.reason: The pronoun αὐτοῦ can refer either to "this word" or to Jesus, since both are masculine in Greek. The word is the nearer and more natural reference, and the sense is the same either way. To "hear" here means to listen and accept, as in 8:43 and 8:47 and of the sheep who hear the shepherd's voice (10:3, 27).

decisions.choice: message ... bear to listen (B); these words ... keep listening (R)
decisions.reason: "Word" here means what Jesus has been saying in 6:35-58, so Balanced says "message" and Readable "these words". "Bear to listen" and "keep listening" show that the problem is accepting what was said (meaning decisions m2, m3).

decisions.choice: mensaje ... soportar escucharlo (B); estas palabras ... seguir escuchándolas (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "palabra" here means all Jesus has been saying (meaning decision m2).

source.text: εἰδὼς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὅτι γογγύζουσιν περὶ τούτου οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτο ὑμᾶς σκανδαλίζει;

records.literal_gloss: Knowing but the Jesus in himself that are grumbling about this the disciples of him, said to them, "This you causes to stumble?

en.L: But Jesus, knowing in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were grumbling about this, said to them, "Does this cause you to stumble?
en.B: Jesus was aware that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were grumbling about this, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Does this make you stumble?
en.R: Jesus knew without being told that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were complaining about this. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Is this making you stumble and fall away?

es.L: Pero Jesús, sabiendo en {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo que sus discípulos murmuraban de esto, les dijo: «¿Esto {{plural_you:los|os}} hace tropezar?
es.B: Jesús sabía que sus discípulos murmuraban por esto, así que les dijo: «¿Esto {{plural_you:los|os}} hace tropezar?
es.R: Jesús sabía, sin que nadie se lo dijera, que sus discípulos murmuraban por esto. Así que les dijo: «¿Esto {{plural_you:los está haciendo tropezar y apartarse|os está haciendo tropezar y apartaros}}?

decisions.choice: knowing in himself: Jesus knew without being told
decisions.reason: The phrase stresses that Jesus knew their reaction from within himself. John often notes that Jesus knew what was in people (1:47-48; 2:24-25; 4:17-18), and the narrator says the same again in 6:64.

decisions.choice: grumbling: the same word used of the crowd in 6:41 and 6:43
decisions.reason: Now the disciples do what the crowd did. The word recalls Israel grumbling in the wilderness, where God gave them manna (Exodus 16:2-12; Numbers 11:1-6), the story behind this whole chapter (6:31, 49, 58).

decisions.choice: cause to stumble: to trip someone up so that they fall away
alternatives: offend, in the sense of annoy or insult
decisions.reason: The verb pictures a stumbling block that makes someone fall. In John it means losing hold of faith: in 16:1 Jesus tells his disciples he has warned them "so that you will not fall away" with the same verb. That is what happens in 6:66.

decisions.choice: stumble
decisions.reason: "Offend" in current English means to hurt someone's feelings, which is too weak. "Stumble" keeps the picture of tripping and falling (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: without being told (R); and fall away (R)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "in himself" (meaning decision m1) and "stumble" (meaning decision m3) mean here.

decisions.choice: hacer tropezar
decisions.reason: "Escandalizar" now means to shock or outrage, which is too weak. "Hacer tropezar" keeps the picture of tripping and falling away (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: sin que nadie se lo dijera; y apartarse
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable spells out what "in himself" and "stumble" mean here.

source.text: ἐὰν οὖν θεωρῆτε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀναβαίνοντα ὅπου ἦν τὸ πρότερον;

records.literal_gloss: If then you see the Son of the man going up where he was the before?

en.L: [What] then if you see the Son of Man going up [to] where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was before?
en.B: Then what if you were to see the Son of Man going up to where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was before?
en.R: What will you think, then, if you see the Son of Man going back up to the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was before?

es.L: ¿[Qué], pues, si {{plural_you:ven|veis}} al Hijo del Hombre subir adonde estaba antes?
es.B: ¿Y qué pasaría si {{plural_you:vieran|vierais}} al Hijo del Hombre subir adonde estaba antes?
es.R: ¿Qué {{plural_you:pensarán|pensaréis}} entonces si {{plural_you:ven|veis}} al Hijo del Hombre volver a subir al lugar donde estaba antes?

decisions.choice: an unfinished "if": the sentence breaks off and leaves the conclusion unsaid
alternatives: what if you see ... ? Then you would stumble even more
what if you see ... ? Then you would no longer stumble
decisions.reason: The Greek has the "if" half of a sentence and no "then" half. Jesus leaves his hearers to finish it. It may mean that seeing him go up would be an even greater shock, or that it would show his words to be true and remove the stumbling block. John leaves both open, and so does this translation, as an open question.

decisions.choice: going up to where he was before: returning to the Father, from whom he came
decisions.reason: All through the chapter Jesus is the bread that came down from heaven (6:33, 38, 41, 50-51, 58). Now he speaks of going back up. No one has gone up into heaven except the one who came down from it, the Son of Man (3:13); compare 1:51 and 20:17. In John his going up passes through the cross, where the Son of Man is "lifted up" (3:14; 12:32-34).

decisions.choice: [What] then if (L); Then what if (B); What will you think, then, if (R)
decisions.reason: English needs a word to show that the "if" clause is a question with its answer left unsaid (meaning decision m1). Readable asks the question outright without answering it.

decisions.choice: ¿[Qué], pues, si ...? (L); ¿Y qué pasaría si ...? (B); ¿Qué pensarán ...? (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the "if" clause is a question with its answer left unsaid (meaning decision m1).

source.text: τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν τὸ ζῳοποιοῦν, ἡ σὰρξ οὐκ ὠφελεῖ οὐδέν· τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λελάληκα ὑμῖν πνεῦμά ἐστιν καὶ ζωή ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: The Spirit is the [one] giving life, the flesh not profits nothing; the words which I have spoken to you spirit is and life is.

en.L: The Spirit is the one giving life; the flesh profits nothing. The words which I have spoken to you are spirit and are life.
en.B: The Spirit is the one who gives life; the flesh is of no benefit at all. The words I have spoken to you are spirit, and they are life.
en.R: God's Spirit is the one who gives life. Human nature on its own can do nothing to help. The words I have spoken to you come from the Spirit, and they give life.

es.L: El Espíritu es el que da vida; la carne no aprovecha para nada. Las palabras que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado son espíritu y son vida.
es.B: El Espíritu es el que da vida; la carne no sirve de nada. Las palabras que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho son espíritu y son vida.
es.R: El Espíritu de Dios es el que da vida. La naturaleza humana por sí sola no sirve de nada. Las palabras que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho vienen del Espíritu y dan vida.

decisions.choice: the Spirit: the Spirit of God, who gives life
alternatives: the spiritual side of a person, as against the body
decisions.reason: "Spirit" and "flesh" stand against each other here as they do in 3:6: what is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit. The one who gives new life is God's Spirit (3:5-8), whom Jesus will give after he is glorified (7:39). The verb "gives life" is used of the Father and the Son in 5:21.

decisions.choice: the flesh: human nature on its own, apart from the Spirit
alternatives: Jesus's own flesh, as if he were taking back 6:51-58
decisions.reason: Jesus says "the flesh", not "my flesh". He is not cancelling what he has just said about giving his flesh for the life of the world (6:51). He means that human nature by itself, and a merely physical way of hearing his words, cannot give life, as in 3:6 and 8:15.

decisions.choice: spirit and life: the words belong to the Spirit and bring life
alternatives: the Holy Spirit, as a name
spiritual in the sense of symbolic, not real
decisions.reason: The words are those Jesus has just spoken in this discourse (the perfect tense: "have spoken"). To say they "are spirit" describes what kind of words they are: they come from the Spirit and carry the Spirit's life-giving work. God gives the Spirit without measure to the one whose words he speaks (3:34). The word here is taken as a description of the words, not as a name for the Spirit as a person; the other view takes it as the Holy Spirit himself, given through Jesus's words.

decisions.choice: God's Spirit (R); human nature on its own (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain whose Spirit is meant (meaning decision m1) and what "the flesh" means here (meaning decision m2), since "flesh" in this chapter could otherwise be taken as Jesus's own flesh.

decisions.choice: come from the Spirit, and they give life (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "are spirit and are life" means in plain terms (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: El Espíritu de Dios; la naturaleza humana por sí sola
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable makes plain whose Spirit is meant and what "la carne" means here (meaning decisions m1, m2).

source.text: ἀλλὰ εἰσὶν ἐξ ὑμῶν τινες οἳ οὐ πιστεύουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: But are of you some who not believe."

en.L: But there are some of you who do not believe."
en.B: Yet some among you do not believe."
en.R: But some of you do not believe."

es.L: Pero hay algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que no creen».
es.B: Sin embargo, algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no creen».

decisions.choice: believe: trust in Jesus as the one the Father sent
decisions.reason: These people are disciples who have followed Jesus (6:60), but following is not yet believing in the sense of this chapter: coming to him and trusting him as the bread of life (6:29, 35, 40, 47). John has already told of people whose believing Jesus did not trust (2:23-25).

decisions.choice: some of you: some of the disciples Jesus is speaking to
decisions.reason: The "you" is the group of disciples who were grumbling (6:61). Jesus does not say all of them; the next verses show that unbelief reaches even into the Twelve (6:70-71).

decisions.choice: Yet some among you do not believe
alternatives: But there are some of you who do not believe (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced drops the "there are ... who" construction for a simpler English sentence with the same meaning.

source.text: ᾔδει γὰρ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ μὴ πιστεύοντες καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ παραδώσων αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Knew for from beginning the Jesus who are the [ones] not believing and who is the [one] going to hand over him.

en.L: For Jesus knew from [the] beginning who the ones not believing were, and who the one was who would hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.
en.B: For Jesus had known from the start who the ones were that did not believe, and who would be the one to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus had known from the very beginning which of them did not believe. He also knew who was going to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Porque Jesús sabía desde el principio quiénes eran los que no creían y quién era el que lo iba a entregar.
es.B: Porque Jesús sabía desde el principio quiénes eran los que no creían y quién era el que lo iba a traicionar.
es.R: Jesús sabía desde el primer momento quiénes de ellos no creían. También sabía quién lo iba a traicionar.

decisions.choice: from the beginning: from the start, when these people first came to him
alternatives: from the beginning of all things (1:1)
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means the start of Jesus's work with his disciples, as in 15:27 and 16:4, not the beginning of creation. The narrator explains Jesus's words in 6:64a: he was not taken by surprise. John says the same when the betrayal draws near (13:11, 18-19).

decisions.choice: hand over: give someone up to their enemies, here by betrayal
alternatives: hand over, with no thought of betrayal
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand someone over. John uses it of the Jewish authorities handing Jesus to Pilate (18:30, 35) and of Pilate handing him over to be crucified (19:16). Used of Judas, a friend and one of the Twelve (6:71), it means betrayal. This is the first mention of the betrayer in John; he is named in 6:71.

decisions.choice: the ones not believing: unbelief among those who had been following Jesus
decisions.reason: The same participle as "everyone who believes" (3:15-16; 6:40, 47), with "not". Jesus's knowledge does not cause their unbelief; the next verse says that coming to him is the Father's gift (6:65).

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb so the reader can see that it is the same word used of the authorities and Pilate. Balanced and Readable say "betray", since that is what Judas's handing over was (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: entregar (L); traicionar (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb, the same used of the authorities and Pilate (meaning decision m2).

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν· Διὰ τοῦτο εἴρηκα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ δεδομένον αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ πατρός.

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying, "Because of this I have said to you that no one is able to come to me unless it is having been given to him from the Father."

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying, "Because of this I have said to you that no one is able to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} unless it has been given to {{gender:them|him}} from the Father."
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} added, "This is the reason I told you that no one is able to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} unless it has been given to {{gender:them|him}} by the Father."
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "That is why I told you that no one can come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} unless the Father makes it possible for {{gender:them|him}}."

es.L: Y decía: «Por esto {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho que nadie puede venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} si no le ha sido dado por el Padre».
es.B: Y añadió: «Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} dije que nadie puede venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} si el Padre no se lo ha concedido».
es.R: Luego dijo: «Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} dije que nadie puede venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} si el Padre no se lo hace posible».

decisions.choice: I have told you: Jesus repeats 6:37 and 6:44
decisions.reason: Earlier in the discourse Jesus said that everyone the Father gives him will come to him (6:37) and that no one can come to him unless the Father who sent him draws them (6:44). Coming to Jesus is believing in him (6:35).

decisions.choice: because of this: because some do not believe (6:64)
decisions.reason: "This" points back to Jesus's words that some of them do not believe. Their unbelief is the reason he had told them that coming to him is the Father's gift.

decisions.choice: unless it has been given him by the Father: coming to Jesus is the Father's gift
decisions.reason: The form of the verb means a gift already given and still in force. Jesus does not explain how the gift relates to human choice; he says both that the Father gives and draws (6:37, 44) and that people are to blame for not coming (5:40).

decisions.choice: added (B); said (R)
decisions.reason: The past continuous form here introduces further words in the same conversation; Balanced shows that by "added".

decisions.choice: unless the Father makes it possible for them (R)
alternatives: unless it has been given to them by the Father
decisions.reason: Readable names the Father as the giver and says plainly what the gift is: the ability to come (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: them, under the gender setting
decisions.reason: "No one" means any person, man or woman; the traditional "him" is the alternative.

decisions.choice: si el Padre no se lo hace posible
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the Father as the giver (meaning decision m3). "Le" after "nadie" is general, so no gender setting.

source.text: Ἐκ τούτου πολλοὶ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ οὐκέτι μετ’ αὐτοῦ περιεπάτουν.

records.literal_gloss: From this many of the disciples of him went away into the [things] behind and no longer with him were walking.

en.L: From this, many of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples went away backward and were no longer walking with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: At this, many of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples drew back and stopped going about with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Because of what Jesus said, many of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. From then on they no longer went around with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: A raíz de esto, muchos de sus discípulos se volvieron atrás y ya no andaban con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: A raíz de esto, muchos de sus discípulos se echaron atrás y dejaron de andar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Por lo que Jesús dijo, muchos de sus discípulos lo dejaron. Desde entonces ya no andaban con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

decisions.choice: from this: both "because of this" and "from this time on"
decisions.reason: The phrase Ἐκ τούτου can give the cause (because of this) or the time (from then on). John uses it again in 19:12, where both senses also fit. Here the two belong together: these disciples left because of what Jesus said, and from that point they no longer followed him.

decisions.choice: went away backward: turned back, gave up following him
decisions.reason: The phrase means going back to where one came from. Those who had come after Jesus now went back to their former lives. The same verb "go away" is picked up in Jesus's question in 6:67 and Peter's answer in 6:68.

decisions.choice: walking with him: going about with Jesus as his followers
decisions.reason: A teacher's disciples traveled with him from place to place and learned from him as they went. The verb is "walk"; the past tense here describes something they had been doing and now stopped.

decisions.choice: From this (L); At this (B); Because of what Jesus said ... From then on (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use words that hold both the cause and the time (meaning decision m1). Readable states both outright in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: drew back ... going about with him (B); left him ... went around with him (R)
alternatives: went away backward ... walking with him (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the idiom (meaning decision m2) and the picture of walking with Jesus (meaning decision m3) into everyday English.

decisions.choice: A raíz de esto (L, B); Por lo que Jesús dijo ... Desde entonces (R)
decisions.reason: "A raíz de esto" holds both the cause and the time (meaning decision m1); Readable states both.

source.text: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς δώδεκα· Μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε ὑπάγειν;

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore the Jesus to the twelve, "Not also you want to go away?"

en.L: So Jesus said to the Twelve, "You do not also want to go away, do you?"
en.B: So Jesus asked the Twelve, "Surely you do not want to leave as well?"
en.R: So Jesus asked the twelve disciples {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had chosen, "You do not want to leave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} too, do you?"

es.L: Dijo, pues, Jesús a los Doce: «¿Acaso también {{plural_you:ustedes quieren irse|vosotros queréis iros}}?».
es.B: Entonces Jesús les preguntó a los Doce: «¿También {{plural_you:ustedes quieren irse|vosotros queréis iros}}?».
es.R: Entonces Jesús les preguntó a los doce discípulos que había escogido: «¿{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} también {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} dejarme?».

decisions.choice: the Twelve: the inner group of twelve disciples
decisions.reason: This is the first time John mentions the Twelve. He does not tell how they were chosen (Jesus refers to it in 6:70) and does not list them, which suggests his readers already knew of them. They appear again in 20:24. The number recalls the twelve tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no"
alternatives: a neutral question: do you want to go away?
decisions.reason: The Greek form of the question looks for a "no" answer. Jesus gives the Twelve the freedom to leave while expecting that they will stay, and Peter answers in that spirit (6:68).

decisions.choice: you also: you too, like the many who have just left
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out and joined with "also", setting the Twelve beside the disciples who have gone away (6:66).

decisions.choice: Surely you do not ...?
alternatives: Do you want to go away as well?
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the question expects "no" (meaning decision m2); Literal does it with a tag question ("do you?").

decisions.choice: the twelve disciples he had chosen; leave me
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Twelve are, using what Jesus himself says in 6:70, and names whom they would be leaving.

decisions.choice: los doce discípulos que había escogido; dejarme
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable explains who the Twelve are (6:70).

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Σίμων Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς τίνα ἀπελευσόμεθα;

records.literal_gloss: Answered him Simon Peter, "Lord, to whom will we go away?

en.L: Simon Peter answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, to whom shall we go away?
en.B: Simon Peter answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, to whom would we go?
en.R: Simon Peter answered, "Lord, who else is there for us to go to?

es.L: Le respondió Simón Pedro: «Señor, ¿a quién iremos?
es.B: Simón Pedro le respondió: «Señor, ¿a quién iríamos?
es.R: Simón Pedro le respondió: «Señor, ¿a quién más podríamos ir?

decisions.choice: Lord: Peter addresses Jesus as his master
decisions.reason: The word can be a polite "sir" (4:11; 5:7), but here it is spoken by one of the Twelve in a confession of faith, and it carries the full sense of "Lord" (compare 11:27; 13:6; 20:28).

decisions.choice: go away: Peter takes up the word of 6:66-67
decisions.reason: Many disciples "went away" (6:66), and Jesus asked whether the Twelve also wanted to "go away" (6:67, a related verb). Peter answers with the same verb as 6:66: if they went away from Jesus, there is no one else to go to.

decisions.choice: to whom would we go? (B); who else is there for us to go to? (R)
alternatives: to whom shall we go away? (Literal)
decisions.reason: The question means that there is no one else (meaning decision m2). Readable makes that plain with "else".

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: The same word the crowd used as a polite address (6:34), but here, from one of the Twelve, it means "Lord" (meaning decision m1). Spanish keeps one word for both, so the change shows only in who speaks.

source.text: ῥήματα ζωῆς αἰωνίου ἔχεις, καὶ ἡμεῖς πεπιστεύκαμεν καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Words of life eternal you have, \v 69 and we have believed and have known that you are the holy [one] of the God."

en.L: You have words of eternal life, \v 69 and we ourselves have believed and have known that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Holy One of God."
en.B: You have words that bring eternal life. \v 69 We have believed, and we know, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Holy One of God."
en.R: Your words give eternal life. \v 69 We have believed, and we know for sure, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God's Holy One."

es.L: Tienes palabras de vida eterna, \v 69 y nosotros hemos creído y hemos conocido que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres el Santo de Dios».
es.B: Tienes palabras que dan vida eterna. \v 69 Nosotros hemos creído, y sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres el Santo de Dios».
es.R: Tus palabras dan vida eterna. \v 69 Nosotros hemos creído, y sabemos con certeza que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres el Santo de Dios».

decisions.choice: the Holy One of God (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the Christ, the Son of the living God
the Christ, the Holy One of God
the Christ, the Son of God
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read "the Holy One of God". Later manuscripts, followed by the KJV, read "the Christ, the Son of the living God", which matches Peter's confession in Matthew 16:16, and others combine the readings in different ways. The shorter, unusual title is more likely to have been changed into the familiar one than the other way round. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Holy One of God: the one God has set apart as his own and sent
decisions.reason: The title is rare. In the other Gospels an unclean spirit uses it of Jesus (Mark 1:24; Luke 4:34). In John, Jesus is the one "whom the Father set apart and sent into the world" (10:36), and he sets himself apart for his disciples' sake (17:19). Peter confesses that Jesus belongs wholly to God and comes from him.

decisions.choice: we have believed and have come to know: a settled conviction, reached and still held
alternatives: two stages, first believing and then knowing
decisions.reason: Both verbs are in the perfect tense, which describes a past act whose result still stands. Believing and knowing are not two steps in order: in 17:8 John puts knowing before believing. The pronoun "we" is written out and emphatic: we, unlike those who have left.

decisions.choice: words of eternal life: words that give eternal life
decisions.reason: Peter echoes Jesus in 6:63: the words he has spoken are spirit and life. Whoever hears his word and believes has eternal life (5:24). There is no article: Jesus has words of this kind, and no one else does (6:68a).

decisions.choice: words that bring eternal life (B); Your words give eternal life (R)
alternatives: You have the words of eternal life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of words these are (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: have believed and have known (L); have believed, and we know (B); have believed, and we know for sure (R)
alternatives: have come to believe and to know
decisions.reason: The second perfect describes knowledge that Peter and the others now have (meaning decision m3), so Balanced and Readable put it in the present. Literal keeps the form and shows the emphatic "we" with "we ourselves".

decisions.choice: palabras que dan vida eterna
decisions.reason: As in English: says what kind of words these are (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}
decisions.reason: The stressed "tú" for Christ takes the setting.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς τοὺς δώδεκα ἐξελεξάμην;

records.literal_gloss: Answered them the Jesus, "Not I you the twelve chose?

en.L: Jesus answered them, "Was it not I who chose you, the Twelve?
en.B: Jesus answered them, "Did I not choose the twelve of you myself?
en.R: Jesus answered them, "Remember, I chose all twelve of you myself.

es.L: Jesús les respondió: «¿No {{plural_you:los escogí yo a ustedes|os escogí yo a vosotros}}, los Doce?
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «¿No {{plural_you:los escogí yo mismo a ustedes|os escogí yo mismo a vosotros}}, a los doce?
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} que yo mismo {{plural_you:los escogí a ustedes|os escogí a vosotros}}, a los doce.

decisions.choice: a question that expects "yes", with the emphasis on "I"
decisions.reason: The form of the question expects agreement, and the pronoun "I" is written out for emphasis: Jesus himself chose them. He says the same in 13:18 ("I know whom I have chosen") and 15:16 ("you did not choose me, but I chose you").

decisions.choice: Jesus answers Peter's "we"
decisions.reason: Peter has spoken for all the Twelve (6:69). Jesus answers them all, and qualifies Peter's "we": he chose all twelve, knowing that one of them would betray him (6:64; 13:18).

decisions.choice: Remember, I chose ... (a statement)
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes" (meaning decision m1), so Readable turns it into a statement, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: Recuerden que yo mismo los escogí
decisions.reason: As in English: the question expects "yes" (meaning decision m1), so Readable states it.

source.text: καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν εἷς διάβολός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: And of you one a devil is."

en.L: And of you, one is a devil."
en.B: Still, one of you is a devil."
en.R: But one of you is a devil."

es.L: Y uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es un diablo».
es.B: Sin embargo, uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es un diablo».
es.R: Pero uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es un diablo».

decisions.choice: a devil: one who acts as the devil's agent
alternatives: a slanderer or accuser, the word's root meaning
decisions.reason: The word means slanderer or accuser and is used as the name of the devil (8:44; 13:2). Here it has no article: Judas is not the devil himself but one who does the devil's work. The devil puts the betrayal into Judas's heart (13:2), and Satan enters him (13:27). Jesus once called Peter "Satan" when he spoke against Jesus's path to the cross (Mark 8:33).

decisions.choice: and: "and yet", setting the betrayal against the choosing
decisions.reason: The word "and" here joins two facts that clash: Jesus chose the Twelve, and one of them is a devil.

decisions.choice: Still (B); But (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the contrast with the previous sentence (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ἔλεγεν δὲ τὸν Ἰούδαν Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου· οὗτος γὰρ ἔμελλεν παραδιδόναι αὐτόν, εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα.

records.literal_gloss: He was speaking now [of] the Judas of Simon Iscariot; this [one] for was going to hand over him, one of the twelve.

en.L: Now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking of Judas [son] of Simon Iscariot; for this [man] was going to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over, one of the Twelve.
en.B: He meant Judas, son of Simon Iscariot. Judas was one of the Twelve, and he was going to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus was talking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. Judas was one of the twelve disciples, but later he would betray Jesus.

es.L: Hablaba de Judas, [hijo] de Simón Iscariote; porque este lo iba a entregar, siendo uno de los Doce.
es.B: Se refería a Judas, hijo de Simón Iscariote. Judas era uno de los Doce, y lo iba a traicionar.
es.R: Jesús hablaba de Judas, el hijo de Simón Iscariote. Judas era uno de los doce discípulos, pero más tarde traicionaría a Jesús.

decisions.choice: Iscariot, describing Simon: Judas son of Simon Iscariot (SBLGNT)
alternatives: Judas son of Simon from Kerioth
decisions.reason: In the SBLGNT the name Iscariot agrees in form with Simon, so it belongs to the father as well as the son, as also in 13:26. Many later manuscripts make it agree with Judas instead. A few, among them the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, have "from Kerioth" in place of Iscariot. A footnote gives the other readings. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Iscariot: probably "man of Kerioth"
alternatives: from a word for an assassin
decisions.reason: The meaning of the name is not certain. The most likely explanation is that it comes from the Hebrew for "man of Kerioth", a town in the south of Judea (Joshua 15:25), which the reading "from Kerioth" (m1) supports. Other explanations have been offered, and none can be proved.

decisions.choice: was going to hand him over: betray him, though one of the Twelve
decisions.reason: As in 6:64, the verb is "hand over", and for Judas it means betrayal. "Was going to" looks ahead to what would happen (13:2, 21-30; 18:2-5). The words "one of the Twelve", placed at the end, show how shocking it was: the betrayer came from the chosen inner circle, as in 12:4 and Psalm 41:9, quoted at 13:18.

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:64 (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: [son] of Simon (L); son of Simon (B); the son of Simon (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek gives the father's name with no noun; "son" is understood, as in 1:42 and 21:15.

decisions.choice: but later
decisions.reason: Readable shows the contrast between being one of the Twelve and betraying Jesus (meaning decision m3), and says "Jesus" to make clear who would be betrayed.

decisions.choice: entregar (L); traicionar (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:64.
